source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

19021.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Josh Turek and Ashley Hinson, Buena Vista County stayed Republican but by far less than in 2024. Hinson carried it 3,156 to 2,546, a margin of about 10 points, down from Donald Trump's 33-point win over Kamala Harris. That 23-point swing toward the Democrats ranks third among Iowa's 99 counties, all of which moved left, and beats both the statewide shift of 17 points and the typical Iowa county's 17. Similar counties moved less: Hamilton 20, Greene 19 and Allamakee 16.

About 5,881 votes were cast, 78% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

19055.t:
Delaware County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved 14 points toward the Democrats. Ashley Hinson won it by 26 points, 4,916 votes to 2,872 for Josh Turek, after Trump carried it by 40 in 2024. Turek won statewide by 4 points, a 17-point swing from the presidential result.

Every Iowa county moved left, and Delaware's shift was smaller than most, ranking 84th of 99, below the typical Iowa move of 17 points and about even with the national typical move of 14. Similar counties split: Dickinson moved 13 points, while Madison and Mills moved 17 to 18. Turnout was 79% of the 2024 vote, and the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

19041.t:

All 99 Iowa counties moved left, and Clay ranks 28th.

Turnout fell to 6,596 votes, 77% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similarly Republican counties of its size, Clay moved more than Kossuth (12 points) and Shelby (15) but less than Crawford (26).
